rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: Housing providers that receive City funding or have income-restricted units under the Inclusionary Development Policy cannot have a blanket ban on renting to people with arrest or conviction records; they must consider applicants case-by-case and may not count arrests without conviction, judicially-relieved convictions, juvenile records, or convictions over 5 years old against an applicant (with limited safety exceptions).
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-history bans; 5-year lookback limit; case-by-case review required
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or that have income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017)
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the housing provider receives DND funding/land or has BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units

rules.title: Boston Fair Housing Regulations - Source of Income Protection
rules.requirement: Landlords in Boston cannot refuse to rent to a tenant because they use rental assistance such as a Section 8 voucher.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental housing in the City of Boston.
